about: Real public files, unmodified except that census_popest_county_2024.csv keeps 9 of its 80 columns (all rows, original Latin-1 encoding). Labels were written from how each publisher documents its keys, before the engine was run on these files. `accept` lists every key the label counts as right.

sources.census_counties_2020.txt: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 FIPS county codes, https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/codes2020/national_county2020.txt
sources.census_states_2020.txt: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 FIPS state codes, https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/codes2020/national_state2020.txt
sources.census_popest_county_2024.csv: U.S. Census Bureau, county population totals 2020-2024 (Vintage 2024), https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2024/counties/totals/co-est2024-alldata.csv
sources.bls_laus_county_2024.xlsx: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, LAUS county annual averages 2024, https://www.bls.gov/lau/laucnty24.xlsx
sources.census_gazetteer_cbsa_2024.txt: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Gazetteer, core based statistical areas, https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/gazetteer/2024_Gazetteer/2024_Gaz_cbsa_national.zip (unzipped)
sources.omb_cbsa_delineation_2023.xlsx: OMB metropolitan and micropolitan delineation, List 1, July 2023, via Census, https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/metro-micro/geographies/reference-files/2023/delineation-files/list1_2023.xlsx
sources.census_places_2020.txt: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 FIPS place codes, https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/codes2020/national_place2020.txt
sources.census_popest_state_2024.csv: U.S. Census Bureau, state population totals 2020-2024 (Vintage 2024), https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2024/state/totals/NST-EST2024-ALLDATA.csv
sources.census_zcta_county_2020.txt: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 ZCTA to county relationship file, https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/zcta520/tab20_zcta520_county20_natl.txt

pairs.note: County code 001 exists in most states, so the county code alone repeats. The popest file also has a state total row per state (COUNTY = 000), and Connecticut's 2024 rows use planning regions that the 2020 code list doesn't have.

accept: County FIPS Code × State FIPS Code ↔ COUNTY × STATE
pairs.note: Excel with a title row vs Latin-1 CSV. LAUS also has Puerto Rico, which popest doesn't.

accept: County FIPS Code × State FIPS Code ↔ COUNTYFP × STATEFP

pairs.note: One row per state on the left, one per county (plus state totals) on the right, so the join fans out.
Five-digit county GEOID on both sides. The relationship file has many ZCTAs per county, so the join fans out, and its first rows have a blank ZCTA.
One row per CBSA on the left; one row per county in the delineation, which has two title rows above the header.

accept: FIPS County Code × FIPS State Code ↔ COUNTYFP × STATEFP
pairs.note: 2023 delineation uses Connecticut planning regions; the 2020 code list has the old counties.

accept: FIPS County Code × FIPS State Code ↔ COUNTY × STATE
pairs.note: Both use Connecticut planning regions. The delineation leaves out non-metro counties.

accept: FIPS County Code × FIPS State Code ↔ County FIPS Code × State FIPS Code
pairs.note: Two Excel files, both with title rows.
The popest state file also has a U.S. row and four region rows (STATE = 00).
State totals against counties, so it fans out.
Places repeat their state many times; the state file is the lookup.
Postal abbreviation on both sides, under different names.
Postal code on the left, state code and name on the right, so the key needs the built-in state lookup (abbreviation to name or to FIPS). The left fans out to every county.
pairs.label_corrected: 2026-11-10, after the first run: the original label was "none", which forgot that the state lookup exists. The first run scored this pair right for the wrong reason (it said no key, and a lookup key matched 3,222 of 3,222).

labelled_before_running: Pairs r7 to r20 were labelled on 2026-11-10 before the engine was run on them.
